title: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Program Plan (Customer Selection + Onboarding + Feedback Loop)
content:
Purpose
This is the working plan for the SIEM-ready audit export (beta). It covers:
- Beta customer selection criteria
- Onboarding checklist + readiness gates
- Weekly feedback questions + operating cadence
- Success metrics and exit criteria (beta → GA planning)
- CS/SE comms templates (email + Slack)

Owners and roles
- Product owner (requirements + beta definition): Naomi Feldman
- Security Eng (schema + security posture): Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
- SRE (SLOs, alerts, runbooks): Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Console + control plane (UX + destination management): Chloe Martin / Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
- Solutions Engineering (beta onboarding + customer comms): Colin O’Donnell (Private) / Fatima Noor (regulated)
- GRC (evidence alignment, customer security questionnaires): Olga Petrov
- Program mgmt (cadence + tracking): Talia Benson

Beta scope (reminder)
Supported sinks in beta:
- Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC)
- Datadog Logs intake
- Amazon S3 sink (including SSE-KMS)

Non-goals for beta:
- Dozens of SIEM vendors / custom field mapping per customer
- Full historical backfill for all tenants
- Exactly-once delivery semantics (beta is at-least-once; customer dedupe required)

Delivery semantics (beta messaging)
- At-least-once delivery
- Duplicates possible (retries, replay tooling, sink responses)
- Guidance provided: dedupe key + recommended downstream handling
- Explicit failure states surfaced in Console + API (destination status, last_error, backlog estimate)

========================================
1) Beta customer selection criteria
========================================

Target number of beta customers
- Goal: 6–10 customers total
- Distribution targets:
  - 3–5 Hosted API customers (high volume + normal enterprise security expectations)
  - 2–3 Dedicated customers (predictable throughput + isolation needs)
  - 1–2 Private deployment customers (VPC/on-prem constraints; validate installer + upgrades)

Selection criteria (must-have)
1) Clear SIEM destination requirement
   - Splunk or Datadog already in use OR concrete plan to ingest to S3-based pipeline
   - Identified owner on security team who can validate end-to-end ingestion

2) Willingness to participate in beta process
   - Weekly 30 min check-in for 6–8 weeks
   - Will share example queries/dashboards and feedback on schema, filtering, and operability
   - Will accept beta limitations (at-least-once, possible duplicates, controlled rollout)

3) Audit value
   - Uses Redwood admin features (RBAC, key management, workspace/tenant management) and/or has meaningful audit volume
   - Needs audit trails for SOC2/ISO/internal security monitoring

4) Technical readiness
   - Can provision destination endpoint/token, network routing, allowlists, etc.
   - Can coordinate with Redwood for test events and filter tuning

5) Risk posture
   - Not a “no failure tolerated” environment (beta has explicit failure states)
   - Understands that export is an add-on pipeline that should be monitored (not a replacement for in-product audit log retention)

Nice-to-have criteria (prioritization)
- Regulated or security-forward industry: fintech, healthcare, gov-adjacent
- Needs filtering to reduce noise/cost (e.g., only admin + auth events)
- Data residency constraints (exercise regional endpoints and private networking)
- High audit volume or spiky traffic patterns (exercise backpressure + batching)
- Prior experience integrating SaaS audit logs into SIEM (better feedback quality)

Do-not-select (beta)
- Customer requires exactly-once or contractual guarantees beyond beta SLOs
- Customer cannot commit a technical owner and security owner
- Customer cannot accept duplicates or refuses to implement dedupe
- Customer requires custom field mapping beyond the published schema

Candidate tracking
- Track candidates in PM-4823 (shortlist) and keep a lightweight status table here:

Customer candidate table (working)
- (Fill in as confirmed)
- Columns to capture:
  - Company / segment
  - Deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - Primary sink (Splunk/Datadog/S3)
  - Data residency / network constraints
  - Security owner + engineering owner
  - Target onboarding week
  - Risks / blockers

========================================
2) Onboarding checklist + readiness gates
========================================

Onboarding principles
- Minimize time-to-first-event (goal: < 2 business days from kickoff)
- Validate correctness early (schema + filtering + SIEM parsing)
- Make failures visible and actionable (Console health + error codes + runbooks)
- Establish expectations around at-least-once + dedupe

Pre-onboarding (Redwood internal)
[ ] Confirm customer qualifies + sinks supported
[ ] Confirm contract/beta addendum language (if needed) with Legal/Sales
[ ] Assign SE owner + CS owner + SRE shadow (for first 2 weeks)
[ ] Confirm feature flag plan for tenant (allowlist/denylist) with Release Eng
[ ] Verify RBAC roles required to configure export in Console (who at customer is admin)
[ ] Share links to:
    - Audit Event Schema v1 reference
    - Sink setup guide (Splunk/Datadog)
    - Dedupe guidance (what key to use; how to handle retries)

Kickoff call agenda (30–45 min)
1) What they’re trying to detect/monitor (use cases)
2) Destination choice + ingestion pipeline owner
3) Confirm scope of events to export (start narrow)
4) Walkthrough: Console → Security → Audit Export (beta) + destination create flow
5) Delivery semantics + duplicates (how we recommend they dedupe)
6) Success metrics + weekly cadence
7) Next steps + owners

Customer prerequisites (what we ask them to prepare)
Splunk HEC
- HEC endpoint URL (incl. path)
- HEC token (scoped to index)
- TLS requirements + any IP allowlisting
- Whether HEC ACK is enabled on their side (if they want ACK semantics)

Datadog Logs
- Datadog site/region (US1/US3/EU etc.)
- API key with Logs intake permissions (recommended: restricted scope)
- Tagging strategy they want (env/workspace/tenant)

S3
- Bucket name + region
- IAM policy / credentials path (or role assumption model, depending on deployment)
- Encryption requirement (SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS) and KMS key policy
- Partitioning expectations (we write hourly partitions; customer should ingest accordingly)

Network constraints
- Private/VPC: egress rules, proxy requirements, private endpoints (if applicable)
- Allowlist Redwood egress IPs (if required) OR use customer-managed networking (Private)

Setup steps (Day 0–2)
[ ] Enable beta feature flag for tenant
[ ] Create destination in Console
    - Destination name + type (splunk|datadog|s3)
    - Configure credentials (token / API key / IAM)
    - Configure endpoint/region/bucket
[ ] Configure filters (start with “admin + auth” recommended)
    - Include: login/auth events, RBAC changes, API key events, workspace/tenant settings changes
    - Exclude: high-volume non-admin events (unless customer explicitly needs)
[ ] Send test event (Console “Test delivery”) and validate in customer SIEM
[ ] Confirm field parsing and timestamp correctness
[ ] Confirm dedupe plan implemented in SIEM (or downstream pipeline)
[ ] Confirm customer has a dashboard/query ready to validate completeness
[ ] Confirm who receives alerts on their side (optional) and how they want Redwood to notify them

Operational readiness gates (before we call onboarding “complete”)
[ ] Customer can consistently observe events in sink over 24 hours
[ ] Customer can run at least one query to locate events by request_id or actor.id
[ ] Customer acknowledges at-least-once semantics and duplicates behavior
[ ] Customer knows where to see destination health and how to request replay
[ ] Escalation path confirmed (support channel + severity expectations)

========================================
3) Weekly feedback loop (cadence + questions)
========================================

Cadence
- Weekly 30 min check-in for first 6 weeks after onboarding
- Optional async weekly form (SE sends; customer replies)
- Redwood internal weekly beta standup (15 min): issues, metrics review, upcoming changes

Weekly check-in structure
1) Metrics check: latency, error rate, backlog, missing events report
2) Customer qualitative feedback: setup, schema, filters, duplicates handling
3) Action items: filter adjustments, destination tuning, docs gaps
4) Roadmap questions: additional sinks, advanced filtering, retention/backfill

Weekly questions (send these in advance)
A) Delivery + completeness
- In the last week, did you observe any gaps (missing expected events)? If yes:
  - Time window(s):
  - Approx event types missing:
  - Any correlated errors in your SIEM ingestion pipeline?
- What’s your acceptable delay for audit events? (minutes)
- Are you seeing duplicates? If yes:
  - Which sink?
  - Approx rate (low/med/high)?
  - Is your dedupe strategy working?

B) Destination experience
- Splunk: any 401/403, 5xx, ACK issues, or parsing problems?
- Datadog: any 429 throttling, endpoint confusion, or tag mapping issues?
- S3: are partitions and object naming workable for ingestion? Any encryption/KMS blockers?

C) Schema + filtering
- Are required SIEM correlation fields present for your use cases?
  - actor
  - workspace/tenant
  - request_id / trace id
  - source IP / region
  - target resource identifiers
- Which fields are confusing or hard to use in queries?
- Are filters expressive enough? What filter did you want but couldn’t express?

D) Operability + visibility
- Do you look at the destination health status in Console? Is it clear what to do when degraded?
- Did you need a replay? If yes, was the process clear and safe?
- What alerts/dashboards do you want Redwood to provide (or document) for your team?

E) Overall
- If this went GA tomorrow, would you enable it for production monitoring? Why/why not?
- Biggest value so far:
- Biggest risk/blocker:

========================================
4) Success metrics and beta exit criteria
========================================

Program-level success metrics (beta)
- Adoption: ≥ 6 customers onboarded with sustained usage (export enabled > 2 weeks)
- Time-to-first-event: median < 2 business days from kickoff to verified ingestion
- Delivery latency: p95 end-to-end < 5 minutes (Hosted/Dedicated target); Private may differ by environment
- Reliability: weekly successful delivery rate ≥ 99.5% per destination (excluding customer-side credential revocations)
- Support load: < 2 Sev2 incidents attributable to exporter per month; no Sev1s after week 4 hardening
- Customer satisfaction: ≥ 80% of beta customers say “would use in production” contingent on GA hardening items

Customer-level success metrics (per design partner)
- “Completeness confidence” achieved: customer can validate key event types present (auth + admin)
- SIEM correlation achieved: customer can pivot from an alert/event to actor + request_id + target in SIEM
- Dedupe working: customer confirms duplicates do not break detections or dashboards
- Filters tuned: customer can reduce noise/cost without losing critical events

Beta exit criteria (to move to GA planning)
- Schema v1 stable enough to publish externally with evolution rules
- Documented dedupe guidance (per sink) tested with at least 2 customers
- Runbooks complete + on-call readiness: dashboards, alerts, escalation, replay safeguards
- Known issues triaged: connector errors and retry storms have mitigations (backpressure/circuit breaker)
- Private deployment packaging validated on at least one customer environment (if Private is in beta)

Metrics to review weekly (internal)
- Per sink:
  - events_attempted, events_delivered, events_failed
  - delivery_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
  - backlog_depth, backlog_age
  - DLQ_count and DLQ_rate
  - retry_rate and top error classes (auth/throttle/schema/5xx)
- Customer support signals:
  - ticket volume + time to resolution
  - top confusion points (docs gaps)

========================================
5) Communication templates (CS/SE)
========================================

Template 1: Beta invitation email (SE → customer)
Subject: Redwood Audit Export (SIEM-ready) Beta — Invitation

Hi <Name>,

We’re inviting a small set of customers to our SIEM-ready Audit Export beta. The beta allows you to export Redwood audit events to:
- Splunk HEC
- Datadog Logs intake
- Amazon S3 (hourly partitions; supports SSE-KMS)

What you’ll get:
- Near-real-time export of audit events for SIEM correlation and monitoring
- Filtering controls to reduce noise/cost
- Destination health visibility and replay support (operator-assisted during beta)

Important beta notes:
- Delivery is at-least-once (duplicates are possible). We’ll share recommended dedupe guidance.
- Scope is limited to the sinks above and the v1 audit event schema.

If you’d like to participate, we’ll schedule a 30–45 min kickoff and then do weekly 30 min check-ins for ~6 weeks.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm preferred sink (Splunk/Datadog/S3) and technical owner
2) Kickoff call
3) We enable beta access and help you send a test event

Thanks,
<SE Name>
Redwood Inference


Template 2: Kickoff calendar invite description
Agenda
1) Use case + what you need to detect/monitor
2) Destination setup requirements (endpoint, credentials, network)
3) Walkthrough of configuration and filters
4) Test event + validation plan
5) Delivery guarantees + dedupe guidance
6) Success metrics + weekly cadence

Pre-read
- Audit Event Schema v1 (link)
- Sink setup guide (Splunk/Datadog/S3) (link)


Template 3: “Onboarding complete” email
Subject: Audit Export Beta — Onboarding complete + validation checklist

Hi <Name>,

Great working with you on setup. Your audit export destination is now enabled and delivering events.

Quick validation checklist:
- Confirm you can find events by request_id and actor.id
- Confirm timestamps align (UTC)
- Confirm your dedupe logic is in place (at-least-once delivery)
- Confirm which event types you want included/excluded (we can tune filters)

We’ll keep a weekly 30 min check-in. If you see missing events or delivery lag, send us:
- Destination type (Splunk/Datadog/S3)
- Time window
- Example request_id (if available)
- Any sink-side error logs

Thanks,
<SE Name>


Template 4: Weekly check-in email (async)
Subject: Audit Export Beta — Weekly check-in (<Week of YYYY-MM-DD>)

Hi <Name>,

Quick weekly check-in. Can you reply with:
1) Any missing events or time windows of concern?
2) Any duplicates causing issues? Is dedupe working?
3) Any destination errors (401/403/429/5xx) or parsing issues?
4) Any filter changes you want (reduce noise / add event types)?
5) One thing that would make this feature production-ready for you.

Thanks,
<SE Name>


Template 5: Incident / degradation notice (if Redwood-side)
Subject: Notice: Audit Export delivery delays for <tenant/workspace> (beta)

Hi <Name>,

We’re seeing elevated delivery delays for your audit export destination starting at <timestamp UTC>. Impact:
- Audit export may be delayed and/or retrying (duplicates possible when recovery occurs).
- Your primary Redwood API is not impacted.

What we’re doing:
- Investigating <brief cause if known>
- Mitigation steps: <pause destination / backoff tuning / replay plan>

Next update by: <time>

If you need a replay for a specific window after recovery, we can coordinate.

Thanks,
<Owner>


Template 6: Requesting customer-side action (credentials/network)
Subject: Action needed: Audit Export destination authentication/network update

Hi <Name>,

We’re seeing authentication/network errors when delivering audit events to your destination:
- Destination: <name>
- Error class: <401/403/timeout/SSL/429>
- First seen: <timestamp>

Requested action:
- <rotate token / update allowlist / confirm endpoint>

After you make the change, reply and we can re-test delivery.

Thanks,
<SE Name>


========================================
6) Internal notes / open questions
========================================

Open questions to resolve during beta
- Best-practice dedupe guidance per sink (Splunk vs Datadog vs S3) — confirm with at least 2 customer pipelines
- Recommended “starter filter set” for most enterprise customers (admin/auth focused) with minimal risk of missing important activity
- Private deployments: final docs on network egress requirements and secrets integration patterns

Tracking and reporting
- Talia to maintain beta tracker (customers, onboarding status, weekly notes, blockers)
- SE owners to drop weekly summary in #siem-export-beta (internal) with:
  - Customer sentiment
  - Issues and severity
  - Requests for roadmap/features

Escalation
- Customer incidents: go through standard Support channel; tag “SIEM Export Beta”
- Internal escalation:
  - Security/schema questions → Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei
  - SLO/alerts/backlog/replay → Sean Gallagher (SRE)
  - Console/config bugs → Chloe Martin / Control Plane on-call

Appendix: recommended initial filters (starting point)
Recommended “starter set” for onboarding (adjust per customer):
- Include: auth/login/logout failures; RBAC role changes; API key create/rotate/revoke; workspace/tenant settings changes; export destination config changes (meta-audit)
- Exclude initially: high-volume routine events not needed for security monitoring (unless customer requests)

End of doc (working; update as customers are confirmed and onboarding completes).
